name: Virginia
source: Primary, read 2026-10-24 (s359): Code of Virginia 58.1-320 (rates) and 58.1-322.03 (standard deduction by year, 930 / 800 exemptions, age deduction) on law.lis.virginia.gov; Virginia Tax 2025 Form 760 Resident Individual Income Tax Booklet (tax rate schedule page 35, Age 65 and Older Deduction Worksheet, standard deduction and exemptions, tax.virginia.gov/sites/default/files/vatax-pdf/2025-760-instructions.pdf); tax.virginia.gov deductions, exemptions, additions and subtractions pages. Earlier second sources: EY Tax News 2025-1326 (HB 1600), prosalarytax.com and ustax.tools 2026 Virginia brackets

filing_tables.note: Virginia has one rate schedule for every filing status (Code of Virginia 58.1-320; 2025 Form 760 booklet, tax rate schedule page 35, read 2026-10-24); separate filers use it on their own income, so MFS points at the single table. Not modelled: the Spouse Tax Adjustment, a credit of up to 259 for a joint return where both spouses have taxable income (Form 760 line 17), so a two-earner joint return's tax is up to 259 too high.

state_base.note: Virginia starts from federal adjusted gross income (Form 760 line 1), so 401(k) and 403(b) deferrals, deductible Traditional IRA deposits and HSA deposits stay deductible as on the federal return; none of the additions on tax.virginia.gov/additions touches them (confirmed primary, read 2026-10-24).

income_brackets.note: 2% to 3,000, 3% to 5,000, 5% to 17,000, 5.75% above, bases 60 / 120 / 720, the same for single and joint (Code of Virginia 58.1-320 and the 2025 Form 760 tax rate schedule, read 2026-10-24); fixed in statute since 1990 (legislated, not indexed), so the 2026 figures are the same.

standard_deduction.note: 8750 single and separate (half the married amount), 17500 joint for taxable years 2025 and 2026 (Code of Virginia 58.1-322.03(1)(b)(v), read 2026-10-24; same on tax.virginia.gov/deductions and the 2025 Form 760 booklet). Legislated, not indexed. The statute as read now sets 9200 / 18400 for 2027 and 9300 / 18600 for 2028 and 2029, then 3000 / 6000 from 2030 (the 2025 booklet, printed earlier, still says the amount reverts to 3000 / 6000 after 2026); later years are not modelled, the model keeps the 2026 amount. Single and joint returns use the same brackets (one table each so the deduction can differ).

exemptions.note: 930 per personal exemption (taxpayer, spouse and each dependent) and 800 more per person aged 65 or older or blind (Code of Virginia 58.1-322.03(2), no year limit; tax.virginia.gov/exemptions and 2025 Form 760 booklet page 9; all read 2026-10-24). Legislated, not indexed.

retirement_exclusion.note: Figures confirmed primary (Code of Virginia 58.1-322.03(5); 2025 Form 760 booklet, Age 65 and Older Deduction Worksheet; tax.virginia.gov/subtractions; all read 2026-10-24): up to 12000 per person aged 65 or older, reduced by 1 for every 1 of adjusted federal AGI (federal AGI less taxable Social Security and Tier 1) above 50000 single or 75000 married; a married couple both claiming it computes one joint deduction (24000 less the excess) and splits it in half, so it is gone at 62000 single and 99000 for a couple both 65 or older (people born on or before 1939-01-01 get the full 12000, not modelled). Legislated, not indexed. Approximation of the rule: Virginia allows it against any income, the model only against retirement income; the income-based reduction is turned into shares of the retirement income at the middle of each 4000 (single) or 6000 (joint) step, assuming nearly all income is retirement income; a joint return with one person 65 or older is treated like two (slightly too generous between 75000 and 99000). Separate filers test the couple's combined income in Virginia; the model tests the return's own.

estate_inheritance.note: Virginia levies no estate tax (repealed for deaths on or after 2007-07-01) and no inheritance tax (state-costs.csv columns estate_tax and inheritance_tax; Tax Foundation and Kiplinger state death-tax lists). Confirmed primary on https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title58.1/chapter9/section58.1-902/ (validation run 3, 2026-10-22).

social_security.check_at: https://www.tax.virginia.gov/subtractions (Social Security and Tier 1 Railroad benefits)
social_security.note: Virginia law exempts Social Security and Tier 1 Railroad Retirement benefits; the part in federal AGI is subtracted (tax.virginia.gov/subtractions, read 2026-10-22 and again 2026-10-24; Form 760 Schedule ADJ subtraction; Kiplinger 2026 and AARP agree).

local_income_tax.note: Virginia counties and cities levy no income tax (state-costs.csv local_income_tax 'none'; Tax Foundation local income tax list). The 2025 Form 760 booklet (read 2026-10-24) has no local income tax line, but no Virginia Tax page states the absence outright, so it stays secondary.

sales_tax.check_at: Virginia revenue department sales and use tax rate tables
sales_tax.source: Tax Foundation, State and Local Sales Tax Rates, Midyear 2026 (https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/2026-sales-tax-rates-midyear/), as of 2026-07-01; groceries and clothing: https://www.tax.virginia.gov/grocery-tax and https://zamp.com/blog/sales-tax-on-clothing
sales_tax.note: Rates as fractions; avg_local_rate is the combined less the state rate, at least 0. vehicle_rate is the purchase tax on a car: 0.0415 from the state's own source (Virginia motor vehicle sales and use tax, 4.15% of the sale price from 2016-07-01, no local tax (Code of Virginia 58.1-2402, law.lis.virginia.gov, fetched 2026-10-22; Virginia DMV sales and use tax page, dmv.virginia.gov/vehicles/taxes-fees/sut, search extract)). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py. Groceries and clothing: grocery_rate is the state rate on groceries (0.0) plus the average local rate where locals tax them (locals: yes); research note: State portion 0 since 2023-01-01; 1% local remains statewide on food and hygiene products; 2026 bills to repeal local 1% not confirmed enacted. clothing_taxable is true (research: yes; Protective workwear exempt only). Set by hand from .claude/state/research/grocery-tax.csv and clothing-tax.csv (s329).

property_tax.check_at: Census ACS 2024 1-year tables B25090 and B25082 at https://data.census.gov
property_tax.source: Census ACS 2024 1-year (B25090 / B25082) as compiled at https://floridaprobateandfamilylaw.com/blog/effective-property-tax-rates-by-state-2025/
property_tax.note: Effective rate: real-estate taxes paid divided by home value, owner-occupied homes. Senior relief, homestead caps and freezes are not in it (a buyer pays the full rate). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

home_insurance.source: Insurify state table for a 300,000 dwelling (https://insurify.com/homeowners-insurance/states/), October 2026
home_insurance.note: Average annual premium for a 300,000 dwelling. Quote averages differ by 20 to 40 percent between publishers, so the model uses it as a ratio between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

car_insurance.source: Insurify full coverage, monthly times 12 (https://insurify.com/car-insurance/states/), October 2026
car_insurance.note: Average annual full-coverage premium. Used as a ratio between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

car_taxes.check_at: Virginia motor vehicle registration and vehicle property tax pages
car_taxes.source: WalletHub, 2026's Property Taxes by State, vehicle tax table (https://wallethub.com/edu/t/states-with-the-highest-and-lowest-property-taxes/11585/), read 2026-10-22
car_taxes.note: Annual vehicle tax on a 29100 car (2026 Toyota Camry LE): local personal property tax on vehicles, population-weighted (WalletHub effective rate 3.97%, the highest in the US). One source, so unconfirmed; the state's PPTRA relief on the first 20000 of value may not be netted out, and flat registration fees are not in it. Set by hand after .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py (which writes 0); rerunning the importer resets it.

fuel.source: Excise: https://www.dmv.virginia.gov/businesses/tax-act/fuels/tax-rates (validation run 3, 2026-10-22); price: USGasGauge state-by-year table (AAA data), 2024 annual average
fuel.note: gas_tax_per_gallon is the state excise in dollars, without sales tax on fuel; average_price_per_gallon is the 2024 average pump price (grade unclear, about regular). Gas excise: 0.326 from 2026-07-01 to 2027-06-30 (0.317 before) (validation run 3, 2026-10-22). Set by hand from the primary source in validation run 3, 2026-10-22; importStateCosts.py keeps a hand-set section.

utilities.source: EIA Electric Power Monthly Table 5.6.B, residential price, January to July 2026
utilities.note: Average residential electricity price in dollars per kWh, January to July 2026 (a partial year). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

housing.check_at: https://fred.stlouisfed.org (Zillow Home Value Index by state) and https://meric.mo.gov/data/cost-living-data-series
housing.source: Zillow Home Value Index by state via FRED (September 2026); MERIC Cost of Living Data Series housing index (C2ER, US = 100), Q2 2026
housing.note: typical_home_value is the Zillow Home Value Index (all homes, middle tier); cost_index is the MERIC housing cost index (US = 100), used to scale rent after a move. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

health_premiums.check_at: https://www.kff.org/affordable-care-act/state-indicator/average-marketplace-premiums-by-metal-tier/, Virginia insurance department Medigap rate guide and the CMS MA Landscape and Part D files (https://www.cms.gov)
health_premiums.source: KFF Average Marketplace Premiums by Metal Tier 2026 (benchmark silver at 40, times the federal age curve 2.124 for 60); MoneyGeek Medicare Supplement Plan G at 65, 2026; KFF Average Monthly Premium for PDPs, 2024; MedicareSupplement.com analysis of the CMS 2026 MA Landscape files
health_premiums.note: Monthly premiums per person, unsubsidized list prices: aca_60_monthly is the benchmark silver plan at 60 (estimated from the age-40 figure), medigap_g_monthly Plan G at 65, part_d_monthly the enrollment-weighted Part D plan, medicare_advantage_monthly the average Medicare Advantage premium. Null means no usable figure; a move then leaves that premium unchanged. Used as ratios between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

price_indexes.source: MERIC Cost of Living Data Series grocery index (C2ER, US = 100), Q2 2026; BEA Regional Price Parities by state, goods and other services (US = 100), 2024, release of 2026-02-19 via FRED
price_indexes.note: Price levels with US = 100: grocery_index is the MERIC grocery index, bea_goods and bea_services the BEA Regional Price Parities for goods and for services other than rent. Used as ratios between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

long_term_care.source: Genworth / CareScout Cost of Care Survey 2024, Ranked State Data Tables, state medians (https://assets.carescout.com/a41bb6478c/298701.pdf)
long_term_care.note: State median monthly costs: a home health aide, an assisted living facility and a private nursing home room. Stored for reference; the model does not use them. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.
